Cervical physical therapy can be an effective treatment option for patients with cervicogenic somatic tinnitus, which is characterized by symptoms related to neck pain and discomfort. Multi-modal cervical physical therapy involves a combination of techniques, such as soft tissue mobilization, exercise, and manual therapy, to address the underlying causes of tinnitus.

This approach has been shown in some studies to have a positive effect on subjective tinnitus complaints in patients with a combination of tinnitus and neck complaints. However, more research is needed to confirm these findings and to identify specific components of multi-modal cervical physical therapy that are most effective.

In general, larger studies using more responsive outcome measures are necessary to determine the efficacy of multi-modal cervical physical therapy for improving tinnitus symptoms in patients with cervicogenic somatic tinnitus. Additionally, more detailed analysis is needed to understand the relationship between cervical physical therapy and stroke outcomes, as well as the impact on other medical conditions such as diabetes mellitus and sleep disorders.

Overall, while there may be some benefits to multi-modal cervical physical therapy for treating tinnitus, further research is required to fully understand its effects and to determine the most effective approach for individual patients.
